page: Microsoft Azure M416s_9_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 416 vCPUs mapped to 208 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with an extensive memory capacity of 8568.0 GB, yielding approximately 20.6 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 4194 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. While single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25%, the massive core count drives multi-core performance into the top 10% tier. This is reflected in high-throughput multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block operations reaching 20,894.32 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 746.92 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%.

The hardware profile translates to high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that can fully exploit massive resource density and parallel processing, though it presents a tradeoff for single-threaded tasks. Database operations and Redis SET operations perform in the top tiers, executing 353.37 million operations per second. Large-scale LLM prompt processing also benefits, achieving top-tier speeds of 43.23 tokens per second for 70B models, though text generation remains slow. This server is highly suited for large in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, heavy virtualization, and highly parallelized data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure M416s_9_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, designed for massive scale-up workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280L processor with 416 vCPUs and 208 physical cores, it features 8568.0 GB of RAM and a 4194 GB local SSD. While single-core performance is modest, its multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth rank in the top 10% globally, supported by AVX-512 vector extensions. This high resource density makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive applications, though it presents a tradeoff for single-threaded tasks. It is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis deployments, and highly parallel data processing.
